summary: Chronological SIEM export with signed checkpoints and rotating KEK (customer-keyed envelope)
description: Issue summary: FinTrust requires a guaranteed-ordered SIEM export to their GCP project with cryptographic checkpoints. They need per-tenant envelope encryption using their customer-managed KEK rotation schedule (every 30 days), and each export file must include a signed checkpoint header that provides sequence continuity (hash chain) and a monotonic checkpoint ID. Impact: Without ordered and verifiable checkpoints FinTrust cannot reconcile events in their analytics pipeline and are blocked from certifying Redwood as a compliant data supplier for their internal SOC controls. Environment: prod cluster serving FinTrust tenant (tenant-id: ft-3291) in us-east. Requested export destination: GCP Pub/Sub subscription with pull mode and DLQ (dead letter) to gs://ft-audit-archive. Requirements provided by customer: 1) Export batches no larger than 10MB (gzipped) or 10k events, whichever comes first. 2) Each batch must have a JSON checkpoint object prepended with fields: checkpoint_id (monotonic), prev_hash, batch_hash (sha256 of canonicalized payload), signer_key_id, signature (rsa-2048 or ecdsa-p256). 3) Envelope encryption: per-tenant DEK (data encryption key) wrapped by customer KEK (customer-managed in their KMS) and rotated per-month. Redwood must accept customer KEK public-wrapping key or use a wrapping API. 4) Schema evolution support: include a schema_version in checkpoint and manifest (semantic version). 5) Replay protection: the customer needs a checkpoint window (last-applied-checkpoint) delivered via a small JSON metadata topic for fast reconciliation. Steps to reproduce / validate: 1) Customer configured SIEM export in Console for ft-3291, set destination to projects/ft-project/subscriptions/redwood-audit-pull. 2) Enabled "signed checkpoints" toggle and supplied KEK-wrapping public key via Console (upload). 3) Customer reports missing monotonic checkpoint ids and occasionally out-of-order batches on their pull consumer. 4) They also see envelope-wrapping failures when KEK rotation occurs (consumer logs show inability to decrypt). Observed logs (customer): "ERROR: failed to unwrap DEK: invalid-wrapping-key-version" "WARN: checkpoint mismatch: expected 0000008f got 0000007b" "INFO: batch-seq 0000008f signed by key ft-kek-v3" Our logs (redwood): "audit-export:ft-3291: publish batch 95; checksum a3f4...; signer key id ft-signer-v2" "kms-wrap:ft-3291: wrappedDEK->key-version v2->v3, rotation pending" Additional constraints: The customer requires transfer proofs (signed manifests) that list included checkpoint IDs, gzip CRC32 of the compressed blob, and a PGP-signed transfer manifest for their archive process.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: verified customer export configuration in Console; the toggle for signed checkpoints was enabled and a KEK public key artifact uploaded. Replayed last 24 hours of export batches for tenant ft-3291 from object storage. Findings: 1) Checkpoint IDs are generated by exporter using a 32-bit monotonic counter stored in replica-local RocksDB; races may occur during rollover after failover leading to transient out-of-order checkpoint IDs. 2) Signature scheme implemented uses ed25519; customer's required signatures are rsa-2048/ecdsa-p256. We accept ed25519 for internal signing but missed schema negotiation step. 3) KEK rotation path: current implementation rotates DEK wrapping using Redwood KMS and expects a single canonical key id; customer provided multiple KEK versions and rotates externally. We surface only the latest wrapping key id in wrapper metadata which causes unwrap failures for consumers still using older key ids. 4) Manifest required fields (gzip CRC32, list of checkpoint ids, pgp signature) are not present in the exported transfer manifest. Hypothesis: two gaps — (A) checkpoint monotonic counter is not globally coordinated across replicas -> lead to out-of-order checkpoint ids during leader swap; (B) signature/KEK negotiation contract mismatch for customer-managed KEKs causing unwrap failures on rotation. Action items captured: - ENG/Austin to add a global sequence service or use ZK/etcd-backed monotonic counter for tenant checkpoint id (design spike). - INF/SRE to implement multi-key wrapping metadata: include wrappedDEK + wrapping_key_version and allowance for multiple valid wrapping_key_ids in manifest. - PX/SDK to add signature algorithm negotiation during export setup (console field + backend enforcement). - Support to provide an interim workaround: disable autoscaling for ft-3291 export replicas for 48 hours to avoid leader handoffs and provide pre-signed historical manifests for reconciliation. Evidence & traces: linked PR for manifest change: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/PR-1984 and console upload event trace: https://observability.redwood/trace/0a1b2c.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial customer report received. Opened ticket and requested recent sample batch IDs and their consumer error logs.

2026-03-10 11:03 - FinTrust Support (customer): Provided consumer logs and a sample bad batch (batch-seq 12345) and their expected manifest format. Mentioned they rotate KEKs monthly via their KMS and cannot accept ed25519 signatures.

2026-03-10 14:20 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Pulled export blobs for ft-3291 and confirmed some batches show checkpoint_id regressions after replica failover. Adding ENG@austin for design on monotonic global IDs.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Austin Reynolds (Eng): Agreed this needs a coordinated counter. Proposed short-term: lease-based leader for export writer per-tenant kept stable by adding a 5-minute leader TTL. Long-term: commit to an etcd-backed counter per-tenant. Assigned to ENG backlog.

2026-03-11 13:10 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Provided temporary mitigation: disabled export autoscaling for tenant ft-3291 at 12:30 UTC and re-published 24-hour backfill with signed manifests using rsa-2048 via internal signer. Sent FinTrust pre-signed manifests and instruction to replay using provided manifest IDs.

2026-03-12 09:30 - FinTrust Support: Confirmed they were able to reconcile ~95% of events after applying provided pre-signed manifests. Still seeing two small ranges with missing checkpoints; requested permanent fix and manifest schema change to include gzip CRC32 and wrapping_key_version.

2026-03-12 16:50 - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Noted next steps and ETA: ENG design spike complete by 2026-03-18; manifest schema change PR targeted for 2026-03-22; customer requested weekly status updates until resolved.
resolution: Workaround applied: autoscaling for tenant export disabled temporarily and pre-signed manifests delivered to customer. Short-term fix: include wrapping_key_version in manifest and add rsa-2048 signer option to exporter via a feature flag. Long-term: implement etcd-backed monotonic tenant counters and a KEK compatibility layer to accept multi-version wraps. Owner teams: ENG (checkpoint design) & SRE (rolling deployment + test plan). Planned release: manifest schema patch 2026-03-22; counter implementation in Q2.
